info.title: service-geokatcher
info.description: geoKatcher monitors geofences between two layers of geospatial data. It exposes a `monitor` service to create, read, update and delete monitors, and a healthcheck endpoint. Layers and features are retrieved from a Kano instance discovered over feathers-distributed.

tags.name: Monitors
tags.description: Create, read, update and delete geofence monitors

get.description: Returns the service name and its version. The version can be overridden at build time with the `VERSION` environment variable, and a `buildNumber` is added when `BUILD_NUMBER` is set.
Returns the stored monitors. Feathers query parameters are supported through the query string (e.g. `?monitor.name=my-monitor`). Pagination is disabled, so the response is a plain array.

post.description:
Validates the monitor structure, then runs the evaluation once before saving. If either fails, nothing is persisted and the error is returned.

Set `monitor.type` to `dryRun` to test a monitor without persisting it, running its action or emitting events: `name` and `trigger` are then optional and the response is a `DryRunResult` instead of a stored monitor.

201.description: The created monitor, or a dry-run result when `monitor.type` is `dryRun`

put.description: Full update: the whole monitor is replaced, so nothing is inherited. `monitor.name` and `monitor.enabled` must be provided explicitly, and `monitor.type` may only be `cron` or `event` (not `dryRun`). The structure is validated and re-evaluated before saving.

patch.description:
Partial update: only the supplied fields change, the rest are inherited from the stored monitor. Two exceptions, because a section that *is* supplied only inherits its `name`:

- when updating a layer element (`target` or `zone`), its `filter` must be provided again to be kept, otherwise it is dropped;
- when updating `monitor.action`, its `additionalProperties` must be provided again to be kept, otherwise it is dropped.

These constraints only apply to the part actually being updated.

delete.description: Stops the monitor's schedule/listeners and removes it from the database.

bearerAuth.description: Paste a Kalisio JWT access token to authorize requests sent through the API gateway.

LayerElement.description: A layer the monitor watches. `target` and `zone` share this exact shape. The layer can be a user-defined layer (e.g. `layer1`) or a built-in one (e.g. `hubeau_hydro`).

name.description: The name (or id) of the layer to monitor.

filter.description: Optional MongoDB query selecting a subset of the layer's features.

LayerInfo.description: Generated by the service to determine which Kano service to query. Ignored if provided by the client.

Evaluation.description: What operation the monitor evaluates between the target and the zone.

alertOn.description: Alert when matching features are found (`data`) or when none are found (`noData`).

type.description: The evaluation operator. Supported values: `geoWithin` (zone inside target), `geoIntersects` (target and zone intersect), `near` (target and zone are close).

maxDistance.description: Maximum distance, in meters, for a `near` evaluation.

minDistance.description: Minimum distance, in meters, for a `near` evaluation.

Action.description: What happens when the monitor's alert status changes. Even with `no-webhook`, the monitor still emits an event on its feathers service on every status change.

type.description: The kind of action to run.

cooldown.description: Seconds to wait before re-sending a "still firing" alert.

url.description: Target URL of the action. Required for every type except `no-webhook`.

additionalProperties.description: Type-specific payload. Required for `crisis-webhook` (see CrisisWebhookProperties) and `custom-request` (see CustomRequestProperties); forbidden for `no-webhook` and `slack-webhook`.

token.description: Token used to interact with the crisis service.

template.description: The crisis alert template (id or name).

name.description: Alert name. Defaults to the monitor name.

description.description: Alert description. Defaults to the monitor description.

CustomRequestProperties.description: `monitor.action.additionalProperties` when `action.type` is `custom-request`. Supports `%monitorName%` and `%monitorStatus%` templating in `url`, `headers` and `body`.

method.description: HTTP method of the outgoing request.

name.description: The monitor name. Required except for a `dryRun`.

type.description: `event` (triggered by feathers events), `cron` (scheduled) or `dryRun` (create-only, not persisted).

trigger.description: What triggers the monitor, depending on `type`: an array of event names when `type` is `event`, a valid cron expression (string) when `type` is `cron`. Not required for `dryRun`.

MonitorInput.description:
The payload of a monitor. `target` and `zone` are the two layers being compared; `monitor` holds the settings.

Field requirements vary by operation: on **create** `monitor.type` may be `event`, `cron` or `dryRun`; on **PUT** it must be `event` or `cron` and `monitor.name`/`monitor.enabled` are required; on **PATCH** every field is optional and missing ones are inherited from the stored monitor.

Order matters for performance: the target's feature geometries are used to build the queries, the zone is then queried. Make the target the layer with the fewest features (after filters).

LastRun.description: Written by the service after each run of the monitor. Ignored if provided by the client.

lastActionRun.description: Timestamp of the last action run.

status.description: Outcome of the last run. On failure, `success` is `false` and `error` describes the problem.

Monitor.description: A stored monitor as returned by the service. It is a MonitorInput enriched with the server-generated fields (`_id`, `target.layerInfo`, `zone.layerInfo`, `monitor.lastRun`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`), which are ignored if sent by the client.

DryRunResult.description: Returned by a create whose `monitor.type` is `dryRun`. Nothing is persisted.

monitorObject.description: The normalised monitor object that would have been stored.

result.description: The features returned by the evaluation.

BadRequest.description: The monitor structure is not valid.

NotFound.description: The monitor does not exist, or a layer was not found during evaluation.

Conflict.description: A monitor with the same name already exists.

ServerError.description: A Kano service error, or any other unexpected error.
